analysis.title: EcoWeek 26.41: 2026 has exposed new risks for the European gas market
key_insights: Europe's gas import dependence is stable, but since 2022 supply is more exposed to global market conditions because imports shifted from Russian pipeline gas to LNG. About 60% of Russian pipeline imports were replaced with LNG, even though European gas consumption fell around 20% since 2022.

The Iran war affects Europe indirectly. 80% of Middle East gas exports go to Asia, but tighter links between the European and Asian LNG benchmarks (TTF and JKM) pass shocks between the regions in both directions.

About one-third of European supply contracts are spot. LNG contracts with flexible destinations rose from 29% to 51% of the total between 2016 and 2025, and oil-indexed contracts fell from 70% to 55%. This makes LNG price formation more autonomous and increases arbitrage and volatility.

LNG exports from Qatar and the UAE fell 85% in Q2 and Q3 2026. Two-thirds was offset by higher exports from other producers (mainly the US) and lower demand in Asia and Europe. 17% of Qatar's production capacity is out of service and LNG carriers are short, so the resumption of Hormuz flows since July helped only marginally.
European gas prices are up about 174% since the conflict began. EU gas storage was 75% full at the end of October against the 80% target (cut from 90% for 2026), as high prices slowed refilling.

IEA scenarios put end-of-winter EU storage at 7% of capacity in the worst case (Gulf exports resume only from end-Q1 2027, cold winter, low renewables) and 33% in the best case. BNP says this would support restocking demand and keep prices fairly high through the first half of 2027.
A strong El Niño should bring mild winter weather in western Europe. Futures markets do not price European gas back to pre-crisis levels until 2028.

In summer 2026, heatwaves and drought cut hydro and wind output, and French nuclear generation fell about 10% y/y between August and October. Gas-fired power consumption in Q3 was 9% above 2025, and wholesale electricity prices in July to September were on average 54% above a year earlier.

Italy plans a price cap on gas bought by power stations. Gas set Italian power prices in 73% of cases in 2025 against a 40% European average. BNP says such a cap is only sustainable in the short term and is likely to be costly.

US markets swung on the midterms. The S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.0% on 5 November, removing USD2.7 trillion of market value, on voter support for AI-restrictive measures. Sentiment recovered after October payrolls of +165,000 against a 70,000 consensus.
The Bank of England raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4% in an 8-1 vote, with Catherine Mann voting for 50bp. Its first hike since August 2023. The MPR sees CPI peaking near 5% y/y by mid-2027.
Eurozone headline inflation was 4.0% y/y in October, a three-year high, driven by energy. Core was 2.6%. This strengthens the case for another ECB hike in December.
Brent fell 7.6% on the week to USD96.8/bbl and European gas fell 7.7% to EUR87.6/MWh on reduced near-term escalation risk. Indirect talks have resumed but vessel damage in the strait is increasing.

The PBOC expanded equity-support liquidity tools and raised the FX deposit reserve requirement ratio to 6% from 4% from 15 November to slow renminbi appreciation. Emerging-market portfolio outflows were USD33.8bn in October, USD31.7bn of it equities.
Brazil's central bank held Selic at 13.75%, ending five cuts and removing easing guidance. Mexico cut 25bp to 6.25% and signalled a pause.

risk_factors: A cold snap at the end of winter would force Europe to buy gas on the market at high prices while storage withdrawal rates are lower.
Gulf LNG export recovery remains highly uncertain. Exports resuming only from end-Q1 2027 is the IEA worst case.
Another summer of heatwaves and drought could cut hydro, wind and nuclear output and raise gas demand for power.
Italy's gas price cap for power stations could be costly given the country's gas-heavy generation mix.
Doubts over AI-investment returns and the US political shift against data-center build-out are hitting equities, especially in North Asia.
France's fiscal path: the deficit may overshoot the 5.4% target and the 2027 budget faces Senate debate.
charts_described: Chart 1 shows EU gas imports by source (pipeline excluding Russia, Russia, US LNG, other LNG) as a share of total, from 2019 to Q2 2026, illustrating rising European exposure to the LNG market.
Chart 2 plots EU gas inventory as a share of full capacity for 2026 against the 2021-2025 range, with the title stating Europe begins winter with historically low gas stocks.
Chart 3 plots European LNG prices (TTF) in EUR/MWh, with the title stating markets expect prices to return to pre-crisis levels starting from 2028.
vol_and_positioning: Gas market volatility is structurally higher because of spot exposure (about one-third of contracts) and flexible-destination LNG, which raises arbitrage between TTF and JKM.
The S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.0% on 5 November, then partly recovered. The week ended with the S&P 500 down 3.9% and the Nasdaq composite down 6.1%.
Nikkei 225 fell 7.6% on the week and 18.7% over the month. MSCI Emerging fell 3.9% on the week and 13.8% over the month.
geopolitical: War in Iran since last February disrupted Gulf LNG exports, with 17% of Qatar's production capacity out of service.
Flows through the Strait of Hormuz resumed in July, but vessel damage in the strait is increasing and indirect talks between the warring parties have resumed.
US midterms: Democrats won a sweeping victory, the largest wave since 1974, on hopes of a swift end to the Iran war and with voters backing AI-restrictive measures.
France: riots on October 17 hit sentiment, and the 2027 budget goes to the Senate after the National Assembly unanimously rejected the amended version.
REPowerEU maintained, with a complete phase-out of Russian gas (pipeline and LNG) targeted by the end of 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Europe's gas supply is more exposed to global LNG conditions, and low storage plus Gulf disruption keep prices high into 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: tensions in the European gas market could persist beyond the winter
